newsitem.title: pakistan: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan press - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan press - Oct 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Eleven policemen, including an assistant sub-inspector, were arrested for their involvement in the September 20 shooting in which Mir Murtaza Bhutto and seven of his colleagues were killed.

- Mohajir National Movement deputy in Sindh provincial assembly announced her resignation from the Sindh cabinet and said she was forced by the authorities to defect her party and take oath as a minister.

- Transporters in the port-city of Karachi announced to support the opposition's countrywide strike to protest against new taxation measuers, devaluation of rupee and increase in petrol and diesel prices.
- The Lahore High Court has sought comments of the State (central) Bank of Pakistan and the federal governement on frequent devaluation of rupee and additional taxes.

- President Farooq Leghari tried to play a role of mediator between the government and the right-wing Jamaat-e-Islami, but failed to pursuade its party leader Qazi Hussain to change the venue of protest from Islamabad.

- Representatives of Pakistan and the United Nations are engaged in their respective and collective efforts to secure ceasefire in Afghanistan between Taleban and the opposing forces of General Rasheed Dostum and Ahmed Shah Masood.

- A budget deficit of 5.8 percent of GDP, inflation rate of 10.8 percent and fall in national savings in ratio to GNP are some of the striking features of the national economy during 19956/96 (July-June).
- The State Bank of Pakistan incurred a huge loss of 11.2 billion rupees on account of exchange risk cover provided on foreign currency deposits during the year ending June 1996.
- Three out of four speakers of a seminar, including the Federal Commerce Minister Ahmed Mukhtar advocated the resumption of Pakistan's trade with India.

- Pakistan's total national debt stood at 1912.2 billion or 88 percent of its GDP at rthe end of fiscal year 1995/96 and debt servicing accounted of for 63.2 percent of its total tax receipts of 46.3 percent of the current expenditure of 1995/96.

- President Farooq Leghari leaves on a week long visit of Central Asian republics of Kyrghistan and Kazakhstan, mainly to apprise their leadership of Pakistan's perspective on evoloving process in Afghanistan.
- The World Bank abnd the Asian Development Bank have taken serious view of the government's failure to disinvest the two state-owned gas utility companies.
- The State Bank of Pakistan has described the performance of foreign banks operating in Pakistan as "better than that of local banks."
